name: Rhyme & Rasam: Poetry of Protest - A Discussion Group
description:
We feel poetry's power when the voice seems to just lift off the paper. This month at Rhyme & Rasam, we will read poems that question, resist, and talk back. 
This is a guided reading with carefully chosen poems. It is designed to deepen your love of words. You don't even have to love poetry to join. We keep it accessible to everyone. Depth of flavour assured!
Theme: Poetry of Protest
Hosted by writer and poet Suchi Govindarajan
What's included:
Tea and Coffee (and maybe rasam)

name: The Landscape Within - Mindful drawing workshop
description:
Our inner world is shaped by thoughts, emotions, memories, challenges and moments of quiet joy. Yet many of these experiences are difficult to put into words.
The Landscape Within is a mindful drawing experience that invites you to explore these unseen landscapes through pen, paper and patterns. Through guided practices, we will move through observation, reflection and flow to create artwork that doesn't aim to represent what we see but what we carry.
Whether you're picking up a pen for the first time or have been drawing for years, this workshop offers a space where curiosity matters far more than skill. 
What You'll Leave With

Three personal artworks inspired by your inner landscape
Simple mindful drawing techniques you can continue at home
A creative practice for reflection and self-expression
A fresh perspective on slowing down with intention

name: Brewing Business - The Story of The Filter Coffee - Journey behind building a premium South Indian F&B business
description:
For our 4th event, the Bangalore Finance Club is excited to host Smita Mehta, a core team member and the face of The Filter Coffee.
If you’ve visited their locations, you’ve likely seen Smita in action—hands-on with operations, managing crowds, and connecting directly with customers.
In this exclusive session, she will unpack how The Filter Coffee built a standout brand in the South Indian QSR space. Discover what it really takes to scale an enterprise from 1 location to 10 while preserving the quality, service, and soul that people love.
Note: You will get to taste some of The Filter Coffee delicacies at the event! 
Limited Seats. Register Soon.

name: Lino Print Workshop - Art Workshop
description:
This hands-on workshop introduces the basics of lino cut printmaking, from carving a simple design to inking and printing your own artwork. Participants will be guided through the process step by step and will leave with their own prints, perfect as small artworks or gifts.
The session runs for three hours and includes demonstrations, supported making time, and space to experiment.
Open to beginners and anyone curious about printmaking — no prior experience needed. Suitable for ages 14+.

What should I bring?
Clothes you don’t mind getting messy in, ideas or finished sketches for designs (found images from books are welcome), and lots of creativity.

What’s provided?
All printing tools, paper, and inks will be provided.

What do I take home?
All finished artworks are yours to keep, along with any unfinished pieces. Participants will also keep their carved lino block, allowing them to reprint at home with basic supplies

name: Formula for Crime - Book signing
description:
A global financial crisis brings to light a unique betting scandal revealing how greed is mixed with the worlds of Formula One and criminal activities.
To combat this a special task force is formed that consists of spies and soldiers from all over the world.
Join us at Atta Galatta for the book signing of “Formula for Crime”.

name: Atta Galatta presents “The BWW Short Story Community” - short story community
description:
The BWW Short Fiction Community at Atta Galatta will discuss
Five Bridges
By Colm Tóibín
The story follows Paul, an undocumented Irish plumber living in California for over thirty years, who is forced to navigate the bittersweet reality of leaving his American life behind. Facing deportation pressure, he spends his final days connecting with his young daughter, Geraldine, culminating in a poignant hike up Mount Tamalpais that captures the quiet grief of departure and the fragile, tender bonds of family.
Read the text and come to the event.

name: Treasure Trove - Teasure hunt for kids
description: Welcome to Treasure Trove! Calling all young detectives to put on your thinking caps, lace up your running shoes, sharpen your wits and get clued in! Follow the trail, crack the clues, solve the riddles, and hunt for a surprise treasure. This special hunt is for detectives aged 5 to 10 years. Let the hunt begin!

name: Bedtime Stories - Storytelling for Children
description:
Imagine stepping into a soft, starry night where time slows down, and the magic of bedtime comes alive. We are bringing back the gentle tradition of bedtime stories just like generations ago, creating a cozy space for you and your little ones to completely relax and unwind together.
Underneath our magical pretend night sky, you can lie down, cuddle up with your loved ones, and listen to heartwarming tales that will carry your children off to dreamland. Just bring along your favorite snuggly toy or blanket, settle in, and get comfortable. Oh, and we have a delicious surprise treat waiting for the kids too!
Let’s share a wonderful, relaxing evening together. Spaces under our night sky are limited, so be sure to reserve your spot today!

name: Ocean Explorers - Activity  morning for kids
description:
Join Fleetfoot Scuba & Atta Galatta for a fun, hands-on ocean adventure designed for curious young minds!
📅 30th August
⏰ 11:00 AM – 1:30 PM
👧 Ages 8–14 years
🎟️ ₹600 per child
Children will:
🐢 Discover fascinating marine life and coral reefs
🤿 Learn the basics of scuba diving
🔬 Try fun science experiments on buoyancy & bioluminescence
🎨 Create an ocean mosaic to take home
🍪 Decorate ocean-themed cookies
🫧 Try on real scuba gear and explore the world beneath the waves
Each child takes home their artwork, cookies, Fleetfoot keepsakes, and plenty of ocean-inspired knowledge.
A perfect workshop for children who love nature, science, animals, and adventure.
Limited seats available.

name: Art for Breakfast 🍳🎨 - Art Workshop
description:
No, we’re not eating paints here (especially yellow, iykyk). But we are eating, creating, playing and making a little art out of our breakfast table.
We know cooking is an art. But what about our relationship with food? The weird food memories, comfort meals, guilty pleasures, tiny rituals and all the thoughts that come with them? Let’s explore all of that through a few very fun, very low-pressure creative activities.
What’s happening?


🍓 Eat, play & create with food-inspired art activities


🎨 Try different creative mediums with prompts designed to get you making, not overthinking


✂️ Everything you need will be provided — just show up, have a little breakfast, and bring your curiosity (and appetite for snacks)


No art skills required. No Pinterest-worthy results expected. Just come ready to make something.
Disclaimer: This is a fun, creative space exploring self-expression through different mediums. It is not a group therapy session.

name: Book Launch & Interactive Author Session: Rub.AI - Book Talk and Discussion
description:
What happens when Artificial Intelligence becomes more than a machine? What happens when humanity itself is at stake?
Join author Rubai Banerjee for an immersive and interactive launch of her tech fiction novel, Rub.AI - a story that explores the delicate intersection of technology, emotion, and what it truly means to be human.
This is not a conventional book launch. Instead, audiences will embark on a thought-provoking journey through storytelling, games, and conversations about AI and the future of humanity.
What to expect:
· Humans vs AI – A fun interactive game to test whether you can tell human creativity apart from AI-generated content.
· Step into the world of Rub.AI through cinematic visuals, character introductions, and a dramatic reading from one of the novel’s most pivotal scenes.
· Interactive audience participation, where you’ll imagine what life might be like with an AI companion and explore the choices that define our humanity.
· A candid conversation with the author about writing fiction in the age of AI, balancing a corporate career with authorship, and the inspiration behind Rub.AI.
· Book signing and meet-and-greet during the final 10–15 minutes, with an opportunity to interact personally with the author and get your copy signed.
Whether you’re a reader, a technology enthusiast, a writer, or simply curious about the future, this event promises an engaging hour of stories, ideas, and conversations that extend well beyond the pages of a book.
Come prepared not just to hear a story, but to become part of it.

name: The Alternate Universe Club - Role playing
description:
For one evening, you don't have to be you.
What if, for one evening, you could leave behind your job, your responsibilities, your social anxiety, your carefully curated personality—and become someone completely different?
A retired spy.
A billionaire philanthropist.
A washed-up rockstar.
A princess hiding from the throne.
A detective convinced everyone is lying.
A professor who knows everything.
A villain who insists they're misunderstood.
No acting experience. No costumes. No pressure.
Just imagination.
This 90-minute interactive experience invites participants to step into an entirely fictional identity and spend an evening seeing the world through someone else's eyes. Through guided prompts, playful improvisation and conversations, strangers become unforgettable characters in a room where everyone has secretly agreed to pretend.
The result is laughter, surprising conversations and, occasionally, unexpected insights into ourselves.
Objectives
· Encourage creativity through playful roleplay.
· Create a welcoming environment for adults to reconnect with imagination.
· Build meaningful conversations among strangers.
· Offer an experience unlike a conventional book discussion or networking event.
· Leave participants with one quality they'd like to borrow from their fictional self.

name: Read A Kitaab - Book Club
description:
Bangalore, we’re back! 📚✨
August is Women in Translation Month, and we’re celebrating the incredible voices of women whose stories have travelled across languages and cultures.
Join us for an evening of engaging conversations, book recommendations, and meeting fellow readers who love discovering stories from around the world.
📍 Atta Galatta, Indiranagar
🗓️ Sunday, 30th August
🕔 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM
Entry is free. Registration is mandatory.
Come for the books, stay for the conversations. See you there! 💙

name: Welcome to The Calling - A workshop for the woman who knows she is here for something deeper
description:
This is for you if your 9-5 job or your business is working financially.. but something within you feels like this is not it.
Stability and security have stopped fulfilling you.
Your Sunday evenings don’t feel heavy because your workplace is toxic.. but because you know you are spending so much of your life doing something that doesn’t feel aligned.
You know that you are here to serve something bigger than yourself. And it hurts to live far away from it!

But this ache is not something to fix. 
It is something to listen to. --> It is your calling!

If you are ready to answer the call, this workshop is for you.
 In this workshop, you will:
• Discover your dharma, your deeper direction in this lifetime
• Understand what has been getting in your way
• Take your first step towards a more aligned way of working and living

About the Facilitator:
Hi I'm Lalitha, a Leadership Coach and TEDx Speaker with over a decade of experience in the coaching and personal development space. My journey into this work began with my own dissatisfaction and disconnection with my career path. Years of inner work and spiritual exploration, along with venturing into corporate and entrepreneurial ventures, have led me to my own Dharma, which has been deeply fulfilling. And I am excited to help you find yours through this workshop.
 
Social media handles:
https://www.instagram.com/transformwithlalitha/
https://www.linkedin.com/in/lalitha-mahaadevan/
Age group: 18 years and above

name: Em No Nahi - Book Discussion
description:
Join us at Atta Galatta for a book discussion featuring Clifton D'Rozario and Angela Rangad as they delve into “Em No Nahi Book”. 
Named after "Em"—the Khasi word for "No"—written by the late Tarun Bhartiya (1970–2025), it combines striking text and imagery to create a powerful tribute to civic resistance and environmental activism in Meghalaya.
About the book:
“Em”—the Khasi word for No—is about a refusal that turned into a rallying cry in Meghalaya, when 90-year-old Kong Spillity Lyngdoh Langrin turned away those who would mine her land in the West Khasi Hills for uranium. Tarun Bhartiya’s images and text distill that defining moment into a moving celebration of civic resistance. 
Tarun Bhartiya (1970-2025) often described himself as a ‘cussed middle-aged Maithil Marxist based in Shillong. Film, photo, poetry. Homemaker otherwise’. From Mithila in Bihar where he was born, he moved to Shillong, where he eventually settled, and always thought of as home. Tarun was an accomplished poet in Hindi, a prolific documentary film-maker, a highly regarded film-
editor, as well as a co-founder and editor of Raiot*, the provocative webzine that emerged out of Shillong.
Angela Rangad describes herself as having 'shared and built a life with Tarun Bhartiya in Shillong, raising three children together, while organising and campaigning around a range of issues that included democratic and workers rights'. She is the co-founder of Thma U Rangli-juki (TUR), which translates as “oppressed people's war”, as well as the Meghalaya and Greater Shillong Progressive Hawkers and Street Vendors Association (MGSPHSVA).
Madhu Bhushan, who will moderate, is a feminist activist, researcher and occasional filmmaker currently associated with Gamana Women’s Collective. She has earlier worked with CIEDS Collective and Vimochana for more than three decades, and has been involved with crisis intervention, community outreach, campaigns and advocacy with a focus on rural and tribal communities.
performer:
Angela Rangad, 
Clifton D'Rozario, 
Madhu Bhushan,

name: Eat, Sip & Paint - ToteBag Edition - Art Workshop
description:
Unwind with a relaxed morning of creativity, good food, and great company at Eat, Sip & Paint – ToteBag Edition by Fitaraa.
Design and paint your very own Fitaraa yoga mat tote bag while enjoying delicious snacks and beverages in the cozy atmosphere of Atta Galatta. Whether you're an experienced artist or have never picked up a paintbrush before, this beginner-friendly experience is all about having fun, expressing yourself, and taking home something you've created.
What's Included
One premium Fitaraa yoga mat tote bag to paint and take home
All art supplies and painting materials
Snacks and beverages during the session
Surprise goodie bag
A guided, beginner-friendly painting experience
Who Can Join?
Everyone is welcome. No prior painting experience is needed—just bring yourself and enjoy a creative, relaxing afternoon.
Leave with a one-of-a-kind hand-painted Fitaraa tote bag, new memories, and a fun creative experience shared with fellow art lovers.

name: Bhujang Shetty and the Lost Treasure of Basrur - Book Launch
description:
Step into the world of Bhujang Shetty for a special morning celebrating stories, adventure, and a little Basrur madness. ✨
Join us at Atta Galatta for the Book Launch of Bhujang Shetty and the Lost Treasure of Basrur, the Game Launch of Bhujang Shetty Presents Basrur Run, followed by a book signing.
📍 Atta Galatta
📅 5th September 2026
⏰ 11 A.M.
Hosted by Vijaya, with special guests Femina Prem, Pradyumna Narahalli and Puneeth Nanjundegowda.
Books, games, treasure, and hopefully enough lime juice to keep Bhujang out of trouble.

name: How Well Do You Know Your Body - A Sharing Circle for Women
description:
We’re often taught to put ourselves last. What do we want? What do we need? What is changing? These aren’t questions we’re always given the space to ask, especially when it comes to our bodies.
Olakh is creating a room for women to slow down and have that conversation. A 90-minute, open and interactive session to talk about our bodies, understand what works for us and what doesn’t, ask the questions we’ve been carrying quietly, and learn from each other’s experiences.
There’s no panel or lecture. Just women, an open conversation, and the space to listen, learn and understand ourselves a little better. The session will also include individual fit consultations with Olakh, because knowing your body also means knowing what feels right on it.
About Olakh
Olakh is an artisanal luxury lingerie brand rooted in Indian craftsmanship, designed for the modern woman.
Every piece is thoughtfully engineered, taking months of design, development and refinement to ensure it fits not just a body, but the woman wearing it. Designed to support, move with her and last through the day, our lingerie brings together technical precision, exceptional materials and uncompromising comfort without sacrificing beauty.
Rooted in India's rich craft traditions, our design language draws from the country's art, architecture, textiles, colours and material culture. These influences shape everything from our palettes and fabrics to our detailing and finishes, creating lingerie that is distinctly Indian in spirit and contemporary in expression.
For the woman who values craftsmanship as much as comfort, and intention as much as beauty, Olakh offers lingerie designed to be lived in. Thoughtfully made, deeply considered and created to become an enduring part of her everyday wardrobe.

name: Tools of Expression  - Wellness Workshop
description:
Tools of Expression is an experiential workshop that explores the themes of hands and colours as pathways for expression, connection, and self-discovery.
The workshop explores grounding meditation, inviting participants to centre themselves through the breath and connect with the Earth, the space around them, and the wisdom of the heart.
As we grow, we are often conditioned to rely primarily on words to communicate and make sense of our experiences. Yet expression exists beyond language. Our hands naturally accompany our stories through movement and gesture; they allow us to create, paint, touch, hold, and communicate in ways that words may not always capture. Similarly, colours  become a language of their own offering us a way to explore and express emotions, sensations, and inner experiences without needing to name or explain them.
Tools of Expression creates space to move beyond thinking and into experiencing. Through mindful engagement with hands, colours, movement, and creative expression, participants are invited to connect with themselves in a more embodied, intuitive, and non-verbal way.
We cannot always heal or understand the mind through the mind alone. Sometimes, healing begins when we create space for the body, the senses, imagination, and inner experience to speak.

name: The Unheard Line - Hindi and Urdu Poetry Workshop
description:
We hum these lines. We are moved by them. And yet, for the most part, we hear only their surface – the melody, the ache, the obvious sense of the words. Underneath sits a second poem, and often a third: a borrowed image, a buried argument, a reply to someone who wrote a hundred years earlier.
The Unheard Line is an invitation to hear that lower register. It is not a lecture on prosody, and it asks for no prior training. It is closer to a guided learning – the kind where a familiar song is played, paused, and opened, until the room realises it has been living inside a meaning it never quite saw.
Urdu is the spine of the session, with room for the progressive Hindi poets, the other tongues of India, and modern world poetry. Ghalib, Mir, Momin, Hasrat Mohani, Faiz, Firaq, Dushyant Kumar, Nida Fazli, Gulzar, Kaifi Azmi, and other poets. Join us for a guided workshop for the appreciation of poetry. 
About the host: Samartha Vashishtha is a bilingual poet, writer, and translator, the author of four published volumes across Hindi and English, and the third generation of a family of poets.

name: An Evening with Dr. Gowher Yusuf - Poetry Meetup
description:
Join us for an intimate literary evening with Dr. Gowher Yusuf, author of Unspoken Words a heartfelt collection of poetry that gives voice to emotions we often struggle to express.
Through an engaging conversation, Dr. Gowher Yusuf will share her writing journey, the inspiration behind her poems, and how poetry can become a space for healing, reflection, and hope. The session will include readings from Unspoken Words, audience interaction, and a Q&A, followed by a book signing.
Whether you are a poetry lover, an aspiring writer, or someone seeking stories that resonate with the heart, this promises to be an evening of meaningful conversations and shared emotions.

name: What Writing Means to Me  - Writing Workshop
description:
Have you ever wanted to write but didn't know where to begin? Or perhaps you've been writing for years and are looking for fresh inspiration? Join us for an engaging evening that explores writing as a tool for creativity, reflection, and self-expression.
Hosted by Dr. Saurish Hegde (Educator & Writer), this interactive workshop will include a short talk, guided creative writing exercises, open discussions, and an opportunity to connect with fellow readers and writers.
📅 Date: 5 September
🕠 Time: 5:30 PM – 7:00 PM
Highlights:
✨ Free entry
✨ Limited to 30 participants
✨ No prior writing experience required
✨ Interactive writing session and discussion
✨ Meet fellow writers and book lovers
Seats are limited—register early and join us for an evening dedicated to discovering what writing means to you.

name: An Evening with Namratha Stanley - book launch, meet and greet
description:
Join internationally published author Namratha Stanley for an intimate evening celebrating Vineyard Melody—a memoir of resilience, reinvention, and the unexpected path that led her from India to the most bucolic vineyards of France.
Our moderator is Deepa Rao Acharya, Writer, Social Entrepreneur, and Influencer. Her event company Lit Spirit is tied up with her Foundation, which aims at bringing about social transformation through spiritual awareness. 
In conversation with Deepa Rao, Namratha will discuss her journey from surviving domestic abuse to building a life in France as an entrepreneur, educator, and wine professional. The evening will explore the making of her memoir, its publication in the United States, and its journey toward screen adaptation.
The programme includes a live conversation, audience Q&A, meet-and-greet, refreshments, and a book-signing session.
Date: Saturday, 5 September
Time: 6:00 PM – 8:30 PM
Event Pass: ₹350 (includes refreshments)
Books will be available for purchase and signing at the venue.
performer: Namratha Stanley and Deepa Rao Acharya

name: What's in Your Jar of Wonder?  - Workshop
description:
Join us for an interactive ArtSpeaks experience by ArtSparks Foundation, designed for children aged 7+ and a caring adult to explore the idea of wonder through visual art, storytelling, and conversation.
Together, you'll look, imagine, create, and reflect as you explore how the same moment can spark different ideas, memories, and perspectives. Come ready to slow down, be curious, and see the world through each other's eyes!
Please register as an adult–child duo if you are attending with a child. Parents, grandparents, aunts, uncles, teachers, or any caring adult are welcome to accompany a child. Adults are also welcome to join the session on their own.
Age group: Children 7+ years old, accompanied by an adult. We are happy to accommodate adults who want to join by themselves!

name: Ghichi Pichi  - A playful, facilitated introduction to mixed media mark-making
description:
Before you rush to make “art”, come meet the materials with me, Jade. Play with colours, textures and explore mark-making. Let’s spend some time in free play, with plenty of materials and other folks exploring alongside us. 
Mark-making can be a soothing sensory way to slow down and simply enjoy yourself. No pressure to make “good art” or be productive. No urgency. No prior skills needed.

name: Divine Delicacies - Storytelling and Menu Tasting Session
description:
Food and faith have walked hand-in-hand for centuries; after all, can you truly separate a sacred ritual from the prasadams that follow?
Step into a sensory journey where every bite carries a story. Join us for Divine Delicacies, an immersive experience where stories meet authentic flavors. Taste curated samples of temple prasadams while listening to the stories behind them.

name: Lahe Lahe Caravan presents Harry Potter Book Discussion - Book Discussion
description:
For hard-core Potterheads age 12 and above!
Get into the minds of the characters, ferret out the intricacies of the plot - enter the wizarding world and share your thoughts and insights!
Will help if you have read all the Harry Potter books - this discussion will be based only on the books and not the movies.
The event is curated by Lahe Lahe Caravan and is being hosted at Atta Galatta.

name: Swalpa Laugh Maadi - comedy, games, and joke-writing
description:
Warning: Contains Laughter
Why do some jokes kill and others die on stage? Author Shaival Thakkar knows the secrets.
Join us for an evening of comedy, games, and joke-writing inspired by his Joke Therapy. No experience needed — just a sense of humor.
You'll leave with: new jokes, new friends, and a smile. Results not guaranteed. Laughter is.

name: Classroom of Life - Playback Theatre Performance
description:
Who do you remember when you think of your teachers and mentors?
This Teachers’ Day, let’s go beyond the classroom and revisit the people who have taught us something about life.
It could be your school teacher.
A college professor.
A mentor at work.
A parent, friend, colleague, stranger —
or someone who never knew they were teaching you at all.
Because the Classroom of Life has many teachers. ❤️
Join Threads & Tales, a Playback Theatre ensemble, for an intimate evening where your real-life stories come alive on stage through spontaneous theatre, music, movement and metaphor.
Threads and Tales is an initiative by Lahe Lahe Caravan. Come to listen, laugh, remember, reflect and connect — and perhaps share a story of your own.
Come with a story.
Come with a memory.
Or simply come and listen.
Because sometimes, the most important lessons in life come from the most unexpected teachers.
Instagram handle: @threads_aur_tales

name: When the Self Turns Against the Self - An experential workshop on healing and understanding the painwhich arises in the self
description:
This workshop re-examines the concept of the "self" from an experiential perspective rather than a purely cognitive one, addressing how individuals experience and understand emotional pain. It opens with fundamental inquiry into how one recognizes when they are not okay and what true emotional well-being actually means. The session highlights a pervasive issue: modern approaches often focus excessively on pain in inaccurate ways, leading to a lost connection with the core concept of self. Instead of treating emotional distress as an abstract idea, the module aims to ground self-awareness in real, felt internal experiences.  Ultimately, the workshop serves as a gateway to help individuals navigate deep-seated pain, break free from restrictive emotional patterns, and reconstruct a grounded, present sense of self.   
The workshop is being organized and moderated by Nimesh George ANd Gokul R who are practicing psychologist based in Bangalore

name: The Next Curve Within - A Quarterly Flagship Experience by The Next Curve
description:
Some of life’s most meaningful transformations don’t begin around us—they begin within us.
The Next Curve Within is the flagship quarterly gathering by The Next Curve, bringing together inspiring voices from leadership, health, longevity, mindfulness and sustainability to help us prepare for the most important years of our lives.
This is not another seminar. It is an immersive afternoon of ideas, lived experiences and authentic conversations designed for those who believe that growing older should mean growing stronger, healthier, wiser and more purposeful.
This edition explores five dimensions of transformation:

Finding clarity through meditation and mindful living.
Building a regenerative future through water and conscious action.
Reinventing life after 75 with purpose and vitality.
Preventing disease by embracing a healthier way of life.
Understanding how healthy, resilient leaders build high-performing organisations through physical, mental and emotional transformation.

Whether you are an entrepreneur, corporate leader, professional, educator, healthcare practitioner, student or someone committed to lifelong growth, Within offers insights that go beyond knowledge and inspire meaningful action.
Event Details
Date: Saturday, 19th September 2026
Time: 3:00 PM – 5:00 PM
Venue: Atta Galatta, Bengaluru
Access Pass: ₹300 per person
Featured Speakers

Cherian Kuruvila – The Quiet Revolution
Vivek Srinivasan – Every Drop Matters
Hari Bhaskaran – Life Begins at 75
Dr. Dharini – Prevention Before Prescription
Keynote: Salma Moosa – Drive to Thrive: Building Fit & Healthy Leaders to Build Fast-Growing Organisations

The evening concludes with Conversations That Matter—a guided networking experience where meaningful connections are built through thoughtful dialogue rather than business card exchanges.
The Next Curve Within is for those ready to reinvent ageing, regenerate the planet and redesign themselves—one conversation at a time.

name: A Little Something - Book launch
description:
Join us for an evening of simple, soul- gripping poetry, amidst light banter and laughter. Whether you're here to recite or to just listen, let the poetry resonate with you as we reminisce over those little things that occupy huge spaces in our lives.
You are invited to the launch of 'A little something' - a book of poems by Sreeja Mohandas, at Atta Galatta, Indiranagar, Bangalore, on the 19th of September, from 6 to 8 p.m

name: Build an archive of family rituals - Art Workshop
description:
Some family stories are told again and again. Others live in shared meals, festive traditions, bedtime routines, and inside jokes—rituals that shape how we remember one another.
Through a series of creative prompts, you'll reflect on the stories and rituals that tell your family's story, then interpret them in your own way through words, illustrations, mixed media, or a medium of your choice.
You can add your work to a living archive of family rituals, built through gatherings in different places, and take your creation home.
About the host:
Presented by Mysticeti, a creative studio that brings people together through stories, creative experiences, and community, this workshop is inspired by Bapa Wants Fish, Mysticeti's new children's book about the comfort and grounding that family rituals can offer during times of uncertainty. Facilitated by Stuti Sareen, founder, Mysticeti.

name: Book Conversations - Book Discussion
description:
Join us for an intimate evening of ideas and stories as Archana Jain (The Human Premium, Fungibility) and Llaher Jain (Sketches of a Heavy Mind) come together for a thought‑provoking book conversation.
Together, they will share their journeys as writers, exchange perspectives across generations, and invite the audience into a dialogue on how literature can illuminate human potential and the art of creating value in a changing world.

name: We Matched, Unfortunately  - Book Lauch
description:
Join us for the launch of We Matched, Unfortunately, a humorous and heartfelt anthology featuring real stories about modern dating, awkward matches, unexpected connections, and everything that happens when romance doesn’t quite go according to plan!
The evening will feature storytelling by the book’s contributors and guests, along with interactive dating-themed games such as Dating Taboo, Do You Know Your Gen Z Dating Terms?, and Dating Bingo. Expect funny stories, lively conversations, prizes, and plenty of relatable dating moments.
